about_the_role: Nexora Labs builds machine learning systems that power document understanding for enterprise customers. As an AI/ML Engineer you will take models from experiment to production and own their quality in the real world.
responsibilities: Train, evaluate and iterate on machine learning models for classification and information extraction tasks.
Build reproducible data pipelines in Python using Pandas and NumPy to prepare training datasets.
Package trained models behind REST APIs so that product teams can consume them reliably.
Design offline evaluation suites and track model quality metrics across releases.
Collaborate with backend engineers to deploy models using Docker containers.
Write clear documentation explaining how each model works and where it fails.
required_skills: Strong programming ability in Python, including NumPy and Pandas for data manipulation.
Solid grounding in Machine Learning fundamentals such as supervised learning, regularisation and the bias-variance tradeoff.
Practical experience building Deep Learning models with PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Hands-on experience with scikit-learn for classical models, feature engineering and model selection.
Working knowledge of Natural Language Processing techniques including tokenisation, embeddings and text classification.
Ability to write SQL queries to extract and aggregate training data from relational databases.
Understanding of Statistics and probability, including hypothesis testing and evaluation metrics such as precision, recall and F1.
preferred_skills: Experience with Large Language Models and prompt engineering for production applications.
Familiarity with Retrieval Augmented Generation pipelines and vector databases such as FAISS or Chroma.
Exposure to Hugging Face Transformers and sentence embedding models.
Experience serving models with FastAPI and containerising them with Docker.
Awareness of MLOps practices such as experiment tracking, model versioning and monitoring.
Experience deploying workloads on AWS or another cloud platform.
Comfort with Git based collaboration, code review and CI/CD pipelines.
qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics or a related field.
A portfolio of machine learning projects, published notebooks or open-source contributions.
Evidence of applying models to real datasets rather than only tutorial datasets.
